=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 390-405 (the new `heal_issue_failed_itself` escalation block inside the `duplicate)` arm of the case statement) | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The escalation block gates only on `SOURCE_KIND`, `EXISTING == ISSUE_NUMBER`, and `EXISTING_REPO == SOURCE_REPO`. It never compares the new report's fingerprint to the fingerprint the existing heal issue was filed for. The PR description specifies "A heal issue whose own run fails with its own fingerprint is escalated", and the inline comment says "failed the way the issue was filed for", but the implementation fires for every phase_failure on the heal issue's source regardless of fingerprint.
  WHY: Consider the intended scenario the fix is supposed to handle — heal issue #42 was filed for a `plan_failed` fingerprint P1 because the pipeline could not plan the fix. The pipeline later plans the heal issue successfully but then fails in the implement phase with fingerprint P2 (`implement_failed`). Under the documented intent, the pipeline is making progress (the plan succeeded) and the escalation should not fire. Under the current implementation, the dedup key `SOURCE_REPO#ISSUE_NUMBER` matches on `SELF_REPO#42`, the `duplicate` action is selected, the `EXISTING == ISSUE_NUMBER` branch is taken, and a CRITICAL Telegram alert is dispatched plus the escalated label is applied. The heal issue is then treated as permanently stuck even though the pipeline is one phase further along. The same false positive fires any time the heal issue's pipeline produces a fresh failure with a different fingerprint. The existing test `test_intake_escalates_a_heal_issue_that_fails_its_own_run` does not catch this because it only ever sends reports with the same fingerprint the heal issue carries (`fp=fp`); a non-matching fingerprint case is never exercised.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_intake.sh:lines 244-257 (the LOG_FILES append inside the job-log fetch loop) | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The conditional that gates `LOG_FILES+=("${FILTERED_LOG}")` for `phase_failure` only appends when the filtered log is non-empty (`[ -s "${FILTERED_LOG}" ]`). On the fetch-failure branch the else writes the placeholder `(job log unavailable)` to `FILTERED_LOG` and falls through to the outer `if [ "${SOURCE_KIND}" != "phase_failure" ]` (false), so the placeholder is correctly skipped. But on the success branch when `filter-log` produces an empty filtered output (the python helper fails and `: > "${FILTERED_LOG}"` is hit), the placeholder file is also empty, so neither path appends the empty file to LOG_FILES. That is intentional, but the comment is misleading: it claims the placeholder "should appear in the diagnosis, not in the fingerprint input". The diagnosis is rendered from `failing_step` (a field passed in the loop), so the placeholder is never read by `error-signature` anyway. The branch is fine at runtime, but a future maintainer who adds another append site for `phase_failure` could re-introduce the placeholder into LOG_FILES and silently change the fingerprint.
  WHY: It does not currently fail. The empty/placeholder path is currently correct, but the absence of a guard `LOG_FILES=()` reset or an explicit comment documenting why both branches skip the append leaves the next change free to regress.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal.py:`phase_failure_streak` at lines ~676-700 | severity=low | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: When `trusted_author` is set but the reporter could not resolve it (the shell passes `COMMENT_AUTHOR=""`), the streak loop treats `trusted_author=""` as truthy (not `None`), so every comment whose `.user.login` is non-empty fails the equality check `!= ""` and is skipped. The post-loop `if current and not current_seen: streak += 1` then bumps the streak to 1 anyway, and `max(1, streak)` keeps it at 1. That is the intended fail-open behavior and is tested (`test_phase_report_skip_paths` exercises the `comment_author_unavailable` path indirectly via `comments_fetch_failed`). No defect.
  WHY: It does not fail.
- tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:the 371 added lines covering `test_phase_failure_streak_counts_the_trailing_failures_of_one_phase`, `test_phase_failure_comment_markers_match_the_workflows`, `test_build_phase_failure_payload_validates_and_carries_lineage`, `test_phase_report_dispatches_the_first_failed_run`, `test_phase_report_skip_paths`, `test_intake_phase_failure_*`, `test_intake_escalates_a_heal_issue_that_fails_its_own_run`, `test_phase_workflows_wire_the_heal_report_job`, plus the autofix default-threshold test | severity=low | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The CI job `tests-heal-plan-and-validation` has a 20-minute budget and currently runs both `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py` and `tests/test_workflow_failure_heal_pr_reconcile.py`. Run 37399765807 was killed with exit 143 (runner shutdown) at approximately 51% progress. The new tests add substantial shell-integration coverage (`_run(work/scripts/...sh, ...)`, intake mocks with many sub-asserts), each of which spawns a real bash subprocess. Some of these subprocesses also run `gh api` through the mocked shim. On slower runners the combined shell-test load can plausibly push the suite past the 20-minute cap, in which case the job would terminate without recording a clean test result.
  WHY: This is not a code-correctness defect. It is an operational concern: if the suite reliably exceeds 20 minutes on the 4-core runner used by this matrix group, the gate fails open and the editor never gets a real test signal. The fix would be to raise `tests-heal-plan-and-validation`'s budget in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, not to remove the new tests.
